newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down as recent panic fades.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down as recent panic fades.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed down 135 basis points at 27.25 percent on Thursday, due to an adjustment after panic over the peso eased and banks deliberately sold paper at low rates to bring yields down, traders said.
"The same thing happened as last week. First they overreacted after primary rate hikes (on Tuesday), then secondary rates retreated," a trader said.
Traders also noted that, although the peso closed weak again, there was no speculative onslaught as on Wednesday and the money market brushed the peso dip aside.
Other traders said that rates fell as banks sought to force them down.

"Banks just can't keep paying such high rates in the secondary market, so they are doing what they can to bring them down. If they have paper they hold on to it, or settle trades at low rates among themselves," said another trader.
Another sign of relief after widespread jitters over the peso on Wednesday was that rates also fell in the term market, traders said.
Secondary 28-day rates, for example, closed down 175 basis points at 27.25 percent.
"The market was notably calmer, although the spread between buy and sell bids is still wide," a trader said, adding that spreads tend to narrow when the market is more stable.
Credit maturities were expected to total a hefty 8.592 billion pesos on Friday.
